Fundus examination revealed obvious the pigmented chorioretinal scars and yellow-white retinochoroidal lesions (1 optic disc size, Fig. 3A). clinician.final_diagnosis: Ocular Toxoplasmosis involving the right eye
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 38-year-old male presented with 5 days of decreased vision in the right eye. Clinical examination revealed punctate gray-white keratopigmentation, positive atrial flashes, light vitreous turbidity, and characteristic retinochoroidal lesions: a round lesion (~2 disc sizes) with clear boundary and pigmentation in the inferior temporal vascular arch, and a yellow-white lesion (~1.5 disc sizes) with poorly defined borders and central pigmentation. SD-OCT confirmed active inflammation with neuroepithelial edema and serous detachment in active lesions, and atrophy with thinning in older lesions. Diagnosis was confirmed by detection of Toxoplasma DNA in aqueous humor and positive Toxoplasma IgG/IgM in both aqueous humor and serum (serum IgG 10.04 IU/mL, elevated above reference 0-7.2 IU/mL). Treatment was initiated with oral prednisone 60 mg/day and azithromycin 0.25 g/day for 4 weeks, followed by stepwise prednisone taper. At 3-month follow-up, visual acuity improved to 20/20 in the right eye, with fundoscopic evidence of pigmented chorioretinal scars and reduced lesion size (1 disc size), and SD-OCT showing resolution of edema with retinal atrophy and thinning.
